newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Commission denies undercutting grain markets.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission denies undercutting grain markets.

text.p: The European Commission moved swiftly on Friday to deny suggestions that a hike in its grain export refunds decided on Thursday is aimed at undercutting U.S. wheat prices.
"It is nonsense to say that we are undercutting the United States. We respect and fully comply with our GATT commitments and there is no question of any other intention," spokesman Gerard Kiely said.

The Commission admits that U.S. traders have complained over Thursday's increase in the level of wheat export subsidies which were raised by around $1.0 a tonne to around $22 a tonne, allowing traders to sell wheat grown for $180 a tonne to developing countries without making a loss.

"We are aware that U.S. traders are complaining but it is equally clear that they are trying to encourage the U.S. government to reintroduce its export enhancement programme," Kiely said. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
